subject: math.RA
name: Finitistic dimension conjecture
statement: For every finite-dimensional algebra A over a field, is the supremum of pd_A(M) over finitely generated A-modules M of finite projective dimension finite?
importance: Would impose a universal finite bound on the resolvable part of a module category.
status_note: This is the little finitistic dimension conjecture; the version allowing arbitrary modules is a different question.

references.title: Xi, On the Finitistic Dimension Conjecture

subject: math.RA
name: Köthe conjecture
statement: In every associative ring, is the sum of any two nil left ideals again nil?
importance: Controls how nilpotence behaves under addition and has many equivalent ring-theoretic formulations.
status_note: A nil ideal need not be nilpotent. The conjecture remains open for arbitrary associative rings.

subject: math.RA
name: Jacobson radical intersection conjecture
statement: For every ring R that is both left and right Noetherian, is the intersection of all positive powers of its Jacobson radical J(R) equal to zero?
importance: Extends the separation behavior of commutative Noetherian rings to noncommutative rings.
status_note: The two-sided Noetherian hypothesis is explicit; many special classes satisfy the conjecture, while the unrestricted one-sided setting is not asserted.

subject: math.RA
name: Dixmier conjecture for the first Weyl algebra
statement: For a characteristic-zero field k, is every k-algebra endomorphism of the first Weyl algebra A_1(k) an automorphism?
importance: Asks whether algebraic quantization retains the rigidity predicted by the Jacobian conjecture.
status_note: Only the first Weyl algebra is asked about. The all-dimensions formulation is not listed, given its relationship to the all-dimensions Jacobian conjecture and reported 2026 Jacobian counterexamples.

subject: math.RA
name: Kaplansky zero-divisor conjecture
statement: For every torsion-free group G and field k, does the group algebra k[G] have no nonzero zero divisors?
importance: Tests whether torsion is the only source of zero divisors in group algebras.
status_note: Proved for many classes of groups. The distinct unit conjecture has counterexamples and is not asserted here.

subject: math.RA
name: Kaplansky idempotent conjecture
statement: For every torsion-free group G and field k, are 0 and 1 the only idempotents in k[G]?
importance: Would rule out hidden decompositions of group algebras and their associated projective structures.
status_note: Known for broad classes of groups; the arbitrary torsion-free case remains open.

subject: math.RA
name: Nakayama conjecture on dominant dimension
statement: If a finite-dimensional algebra A has infinite dominant dimension, meaning every term of a minimal injective resolution of the left regular module A is projective, must A be self-injective?
importance: Would connect an infinite homological approximation property to a rigid structural conclusion.
status_note: The unrestricted finite-dimensional-algebra case is open; many representation-finite and other special cases are known.

references.title: Enomoto and Marczinzik, On the homological conjectures for Artin algebras

subject: math.RA
name: Cartan determinant conjecture
statement: If a finite-dimensional algebra A over an algebraically closed field has finite global dimension, must the determinant of its Cartan matrix be 1?
importance: Predicts an exact integral numerical constraint on finite projective resolutions.
status_note: The determinant is known to be a unit, hence ±1, under these hypotheses; the conjecture requires the positive sign.

references.title: Cartan Determinants in algebraic geometry (classical conjecture and its dg analogue)

subject: math.RA
name: Auslander–Reiten conjecture for finite-dimensional algebras
statement: For a finite-dimensional algebra A and a finitely generated left A-module M, does Ext_A^i(M,M ⊕ A)=0 for every i>0 imply that M is projective?
importance: Would characterize projective modules by the vanishing of their self-extensions and dual extensions.
status_note: Open for arbitrary finite-dimensional algebras; the analogous commutative-local formulation is separately listed in commutative algebra.

references.title: Enomoto and Marczinzik, On the homological conjectures for Artin algebras

subject: math.RA
name: Han’s Hochschild-homology conjecture
statement: For a finite-dimensional algebra A over a field, does HH_n(A)=0 for all sufficiently large n imply that A has finite global dimension?
importance: Would make Hochschild homology a detector of the singularity of an algebra.
status_note: This is the homology conjecture. The analogous claim using Hochschild cohomology is false in general.

references.title: da Costa Cruz, A Survey on Han’s Conjecture
